newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Leftists call off APEC summit protest cavalcades.
newsitem.headline: Leftists call off APEC summit protest cavalcades.

text.p: Leaders of thousands of anti-APEC leftist protesters said on Monday they were calling of protest cavalcades to the APEC summit venue in Subic Bay because it would be "suicidal".
More than 7,000 protesters set out from the Philippine capital Manila on Sunday for Subic Bay, 80 km (50 miles) to the north, but numerous police roadblocks and rain delayed their progress.

Police General Edgardo Aglipay, commander of riot police who set up blockades to prevent the protesters from reaching the summit site, earlier told Philippine radio after talking with the protesters that his men were ready to die to stop the march.

Most of the estimated 7,000 protesters were in distinctive "jeepneys" -- colourful minibuses modelled on World War Two jeeps -- flying streamers with slogans decrying the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum.

"Considering the large number of our enemy, we will not sacrifice our bodies, we will not sacrifice our force because that will be suicide," leftist leader Nathaniel Santiag told protesters assembled at Dinaluphan town, about 20 km (12 miles) from Olongapo city where the summit venue is located.

Chief rally organiser Satur Ocampo said it was difficult to penetrate the police blockade. "We are realistic enough to recognise that we cannot break through this last barricade," Ocampo told reporters, referring to columns of police blocking the protesters' path with a crane, empty passenger buses and dumptrucks.
